name: Fuzzing & Automated Testing
description: Fuzzing techniques, coverage-guided testing, and bug-finding pipelines.

uss.narrative:
The earliest works in this set tackle a core limitation of plain greybox fuzzing: getting past hard, structured input checks. QSYM: A Practical Concolic Execution Engine Tailored for Hybrid Fuzzing (USENIX 2018) made hybrid fuzzing practical by building a fast concolic engine to solve the branch constraints that coverage-guided fuzzers stall on, while MoonShine (USENIX 2018) attacked the same "where do good seeds come from" problem for OS kernel fuzzers via trace distillation. Alongside these, the community began pushing fuzzing into domains that resist naive byte mutation — embedded firmware in Inception (USENIX 2018) — setting up two enduring themes: smarter input reasoning, and re-hosting hard-to-run targets.

The 2019-2020 wave is dominated by two breakthroughs. First, making the fuzzer itself smarter about program semantics: GRIMOIRE (USENIX 2019) synthesizes input structure on the fly, GREYONE (USENIX 2020) uses data-flow/taint to learn which input bytes matter, EcoFuzz (USENIX 2020) reframes seed scheduling as a multi-armed bandit problem, and Montage (USENIX 2020) brings neural language models to JavaScript-engine fuzzing. FuzzGen (USENIX 2020) automated the tedious step of writing fuzz harnesses for libraries. Second, an explosion of domain-specific fuzzing infrastructure: FIRM-AFL (USENIX 2019) and HALucinator (USENIX 2020) made IoT firmware fuzzable through augmented emulation and abstraction-layer re-hosting, while USBFuzz (USENIX 2020) and Frankenstein (USENIX 2020) reached into USB drivers and Bluetooth stacks. RVFuzzer (USENIX 2019) extended the idea to robotic-vehicle control logic, and AURORA (USENIX 2020) addressed the downstream pipeline problem of automatically explaining the many crashes fuzzers produce.

By 2021-2022 the field matured along three fronts. Directed and feedback-rich fuzzing sharpened with Constraint-guided Directed Greybox Fuzzing (USENIX 2021), FuzzGuard's deep-learning input filtering (USENIX 2020), and The Use of Likely Invariants as Feedback for Fuzzers (USENIX 2021). Learning-based control matured with SyzVegas (USENIX 2021), which used reinforcement learning to tune kernel fuzzing decisions. Infrastructure kept advancing: Nyx (USENIX 2021) enabled hypervisor fuzzing with fast snapshots, Breaking Through Binaries (USENIX 2021) brought compiler-quality instrumentation to binary-only targets, and Fuzzware (USENIX 2022) refined firmware fuzzing with precise MMIO modeling. Stateful Greybox Fuzzing (USENIX 2022) and earlier protocol state fuzzing work tackled reactive, stateful systems, and TheHuzz (USENIX 2022) pushed fuzzing down to processor instruction verification.

Most recently the targets themselves have shifted: LLM-Fuzzer (USENIX 2024) repurposes the fuzzing mindset to scale assessment of large-language-model jailbreaks, signaling that the area's core ideas — coverage-style feedback, automated mutation, and bug-finding pipelines — are now being applied well beyond traditional software, even to AI systems.

ndss.narrative:
The earliest work in this list is about reaching targets that ordinary fuzzers could not touch. At NDSS 2018, IoTFuzzer: Discovering Memory Corruptions in IoT Through App-based Fuzzing (2018) drove embedded devices through their companion phone apps, while What You Corrupt Is Not What You Crash: Challenges in Fuzzing Embedded Devices (2018) laid bare why embedded fuzzing is so hard, since a memory corruption on a microcontroller often produces no crash at all. Alongside them, more classical concerns appeared: enhancing memory-error detection for fuzz testing (2018) and model-guided attack discovery in TCP congestion control (2018). The theme of the period was expanding fuzzing's reach past well-behaved desktop programs.

The next breakthrough was making coverage-guided fuzzing smarter about getting past hard input checks. REDQUEEN: Fuzzing with Input-to-State Correspondence (NDSS 2019) showed that a cheap trick, matching input bytes to values seen in comparisons, could clear magic-byte and checksum barriers that once demanded heavyweight symbolic execution. In parallel a structure-aware branch grew up: NAUTILUS: Fishing for Deep Bugs with Grammars (2019) and CodeAlchemist (2019) used grammars and semantics to reach deep logic in parsers and JavaScript engines, and hybrid fuzzing matured through Send Hardest Problems My Way (2019) and later HFL: Hybrid Fuzzing on the Linux Kernel (NDSS 2020). Around 2020 and 2021 the field also specialized by target and by decision-making: HYPER-CUBE (2020) for hypervisors, WINNIE (2021) for Windows apps, PGFUZZ (2021) for robotic vehicles, and Reinforcement Learning-based Hierarchical Seed Scheduling (2021), which reframed the fuzzer's core scheduling choices as a learning problem.

From 2022 onward the work became both more domain-specific and more state-aware. FirmWire (2022) tackled cellular baseband firmware, EMS (2022) mined mutation history, and LOKI (NDSS 2023) fuzzed blockchain consensus with awareness of protocol state, while No Grammar, No Problem (2023) attacked the Linux kernel without hand-written system-call descriptions. Engine and compiler fuzzing kept advancing through FUZZILLI: Fuzzing for JavaScript JIT Compiler Vulnerabilities (NDSS 2023) and DUMPLING (2025) for differential JS-engine testing, and testing spread to new compiler-like targets with MTZK (2025) for zero-knowledge compilers.

The most recent turn is toward large language models and hardware. Large Language Model guided Protocol Fuzzing (NDSS 2024) showed LLMs could recover protocol structure without a formal spec, and the 2026 cohort makes that direction concrete: An LLM-Driven Fuzzing Framework for Detecting Logic Instruction Bugs in PLCs (2026) and FirmAgent (2026) pair LLM agents with fuzzing for industrial and IoT firmware. At the same time a strong silicon-level thread has emerged, with ReFuzz: Reusing Tests for Processor Fuzzing with Contextual Bandits (2026), HyperMirage (2026) on hybrid virtual-CPU fuzzing, Fuzzilicon (2026) as a post-silicon microcode-guided x86 fuzzer, and PortRush (2026) hunting write-port-contention side channels through hardware fuzzing. Rehosting also continues to mature with User-Space Dependency-Aware Rehosting for Linux-Based Firmware Binaries (2026). Today the area spans from LLM-assisted, spec-free bug hunting down to the CPU pipeline itself.

sp.narrative:
The earliest work in this list treats fuzzing as a search problem and asks how to make that search smarter rather than merely faster. Angora (S&P 2018) argued that random mutation wastes most of its effort, and replaced it with a principled, gradient-guided search that solves branch constraints directly; CollAFL (S&P 2018) attacked a quieter bottleneck, the hash collisions that make coverage feedback lie about which paths are new. T-Fuzz (S&P 2018) took the opposite tack, transforming the program itself to strip away checks that block shallow inputs. Together they frame the central tension of the era: coverage feedback is powerful but noisy and expensive.

The next wave, 2019 to 2020, pushed on both intelligence and cost. NEUZZ (S&P 2019) brought neural networks in to approximate program behavior and smooth the search landscape, while Full-Speed Fuzzing (S&P 2019) went the other way and slashed instrumentation overhead by tracing only newly discovered coverage. Meanwhile the community specialized: Razzer (S&P 2019) and Krace (S&P 2020) targeted kernel and file-system data races, ProFuzzer (S&P 2019) inferred input structure on the fly, and hybrid approaches that pair fuzzing with concolic execution matured through SAVIOR (S&P 2020) and Pangolin (S&P 2020). Ijon (S&P 2020) made the influential point that a little human insight, injected as annotations, lets a fuzzer break through deep state-space walls that blind coverage never scales.

From 2021 onward the field fragments into targets and precision. Binary-only fuzzing advanced through RetroWrite (S&P 2020) and StochFuzz (S&P 2021); hardware, firmware and peripherals got dedicated engines in DifuzzRTL (S&P 2021), DICE (S&P 2021) and FuzzUSB (S&P 2022); and directed fuzzing became its own subfield, with BEACON (S&P 2022) adding provable path pruning and SelectFuzz (S&P 2023) selectively exploring only relevant paths. PATA (S&P 2022) sharpened taint analysis to crack hard constraints. By 2024 the discipline turned reflective and generative at once: SoK: Prudent Evaluation Practices for Fuzzing (S&P 2024) called out sloppy benchmarking and set standards for honest comparison, even as LLMIF (S&P 2024) began wiring large language models into the fuzzing loop for IoT protocols.

The most recent 2026 work shows the LLM turn in full force alongside a return to old, hard domains. Specializing Language Models for Textual Fuzzing via Reinforcement Learning (S&P 2026) trains models to attack structured targets like compilers, deepSURF (S&P 2026) uses LLM-augmented harnesses to hunt Rust memory-safety bugs, Jazzer (S&P 2026) chases semantic vulnerabilities across the Java ecosystem, and Agentic Concolic Execution (S&P 2026) reframes symbolic reasoning as an agent-driven process. At the same time, a cluster of systems papers extends fuzzing into stubborn physical and networked settings: Fizzle (S&P 2026) for deterministic network fuzzing, Camveil (S&P 2026) for multi-protocol security cameras, Batch Me If You Can (S&P 2026) for RPKI at scale, Stop Starving or Stuffing Me (S&P 2026) for firmware input delivery, and Fuzzing the Physical Space (S&P 2026) for black-box industrial control systems. The area now stands at a fusion point: learned, LLM-driven generation on one side, and rigorous, domain-specialized engineering on the other.

ccs.narrative:
Fuzzing at CCS has progressed from methodology critique to domain-specific fuzzers and finally to AI-augmented test generation. The watershed paper was Evaluating Fuzz Testing (CCS 2018), which exposed that prior fuzzer comparisons lacked statistical rigor and established evaluation standards the community adopted broadly. Hawkeye: Towards a Desired Directed Grey-box Fuzzer (CCS 2018) answered the need for targeted fuzzing toward specific vulnerability sites.

The 2019-2020 period diversified fuzzing targets. Matryoshka: Fuzzing Deeply Nested Branches (CCS 2019) solved the constraint-depth problem using taint analysis and ODE-based path prioritization. Learning to Fuzz from Symbolic Execution with Application to Smart Contracts (CCS 2019) demonstrated how learned fuzzing policies can transfer symbolic execution insights to coverage-guided fuzzers. SQUIRREL (CCS 2020) applied language-aware feedback to fuzz DBMS parsers, and Snipuzz (CCS 2021) tackled black-box IoT firmware without source code.

The 2022 era produced infrastructure and specialization. LibAFL: A Framework to Build Modular and Reusable Fuzzers (CCS 2022) gave researchers a composable toolkit for building custom fuzzing pipelines, while DriveFuzz: Discovering Autonomous Driving Bugs through Driving Quality-Guided Fuzzing (CCS 2022) used driving quality metrics as a feedback signal to find AV safety bugs, extending fuzzing from correctness to physical safety.

top4.narrative:
The earliest work on this list is really about making coverage-guided fuzzing smarter than blind random mutation. By 2018 the community had a working recipe (AFL-style feedback), so the papers here attack its weak spots: Angora: Efficient Fuzzing by Principled Search (S&P 2018) uses gradient-descent-style search over input bytes to solve hard branch conditions, CollAFL: Path Sensitive Fuzzing (S&P 2018) fixes coverage hash collisions that hid real paths, and QSYM (USENIX 2018) makes concolic execution fast enough to pair with a fuzzer in "hybrid" mode. Alongside these efficiency gains, Evaluating Fuzz Testing (CCS 2018) delivered a sobering methodological warning that most fuzzing papers ran too few trials and cherry-picked seeds, setting evaluation standards the field still cites. A parallel thread pushed fuzzing off the desktop and onto hard-to-reach targets: IoTFuzzer (NDSS 2018), MoonShine (USENIX 2018, OS system calls), and embedded work like Inception (USENIX 2018) and What You Corrupt Is Not What You Crash (NDSS 2018).

Around 2019-2020 the breakthroughs came from teaching fuzzers about program structure and data. REDQUEEN: Fuzzing with Input-to-State Correspondence (NDSS 2019) showed you could crack magic-byte and checksum comparisons cheaply by watching how input bytes reappear in program state, largely closing the gap that concolic engines were needed for. Grammar- and semantics-aware generation matured for structured targets in NAUTILUS (NDSS 2019) and CodeAlchemist (NDSS 2019, JavaScript engines), while GREYONE: Data Flow Sensitive Fuzzing (USENIX 2020) used lightweight taint to decide which bytes to mutate. Machine learning entered the loop through NEUZZ (S&P 2019), which approximates program behavior with a neural net, and FuzzGuard (USENIX 2020), which learns to drop inputs that can't reach a target. Meanwhile the field kept broadening its reach and rigor: hybrid and bug-directed testing (SAVIOR, S&P 2020; HFL on the Linux kernel, NDSS 2020), race and kernel bugs (Razzer, S&P 2019), instrumentation for binaries (RetroWrite, S&P 2020), automatic harnessing (FuzzGen, USENIX 2020), smarter scheduling (EcoFuzz, USENIX 2020), and firmware re-hosting (HALucinator, USENIX 2020; FIRM-AFL, USENIX 2019).

By the early 2020s the work consolidated around usability and steering. Directed fuzzing, first framed by Hawkeye (CCS 2018), got a rigorous footing in BEACON: Directed Grey-Box Fuzzing with Provable Path Pruning (S&P 2022), and LibAFL (CCS 2022) turned the accumulated tricks into a modular, reusable framework rather than one-off forks. IoT and black-box targets stayed a live problem (Snipuzz, CCS 2021).

The most recent work marks two clear shifts. First, large language models are now driving input generation and orchestration: Large Language Model guided Protocol Fuzzing (NDSS 2024) uses an LLM to infer protocol structure without a specification, and the 2026 crop pushes this further into agents and industrial domains with FirmAgent: Leveraging Fuzzing to Assist LLM Agents with IoT Firmware Vulnerability Discovery (NDSS 2026), An LLM-Driven Fuzzing Framework for Detecting Logic Instruction Bugs in PLCs (NDSS 2026), and MUTATO: Enhancing Fuzz Drivers with Adaptive API Option Mutation (NDSS 2026). Second, fuzzing has moved down the stack into silicon and CPUs, with Fuzzilicon: A Post-Silicon Microcode-Guided x86 CPU Fuzzer (NDSS 2026), PortRush (NDSS 2026, hardware side-channel bugs), HyperMirage (NDSS 2026, hybrid virtual-CPU fuzzing), and ReFuzz: Reusing Tests for Processor Fuzzing with Contextual Bandits (NDSS 2026) — while classic software targets like databases (Efficiently Detecting DBMS Bugs through Bottom-up Syntax-based SQL Generation, NDSS 2026) and RTOS kernels (RTCON, NDSS 2026) still see active work. The through-line is unchanged: get past hard input barriers to reach deeper code, but the frontier has expanded from desktop programs to firmware, hardware, and LLM-guided pipelines.
